tob-10467: Jonathan Edwards was the fiery New England preacher whose sermons — including the famous ‘Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God’ — ignited America’s Great Awakening. This selection gathers his most powerful addresses, where brilliant theology meets urgent calls to repentance. Edwards remains one of the towering minds of American religion, a philosopher in the pulpit.
tob-0167: The Poetic Edda strings the old Norse lays — the seeress’s foretelling of Ragnarok, Odin’s rede, the lays of Sigurd and the gods. These nameless poems are Norse myth’s wellhead. This Englishing bears their stark might to new readers.
tob-4067: This entry gives the Rig-Veda in its own Sanskrit — the thousand and twenty-eight hymns that are Hinduism’s oldest scripture, sung above three thousand years ago. The text keeps the word-for-word chant of three thousand years. For Sanskrit learners and scholars it is the one needful source.
tob-10267: Waite’s translation of Lévi’s Transcendental Magic brings the founding text of modern occultism to English readers. Its two parts lay out magical doctrine and ritual — Kabbalah, tarot, and the astral light. The book shaped the entire occult revival. It remains essential for students of the Western mysteries.
tob-14467: C. W. Leadbeater’s Man: Whence, Whither, and How is the God-wisdom tale of man’s unfolding — the soul’s long fare through world-rounds and root-breeds. His far-seeing probings gripped 1900s readers. Few books show the fellowship’s world-dream so bright. The book stays a true God-wisdom mark.
cia-0000102967: A July 1982 cable on reports that the Soviets used forced labor to build pipelines, marked as alleged because the evidence was not confirmed. It sits alongside a near-twin report from the same month, showing how fragmentary tips arrived from multiple channels. Together they illustrate intelligence work at its most careful: flagging serious claims while admitting doubt.
cia-0000106267: A September 1964 report on a proposed fake coup by Laotian General Phoumi and Prime Minister Souvanna Phouma. A staged coup — a show of force meant to look real — was a classic tool for reshuffling power without actual fighting. The document opens a window onto the theater of Cold War politics in tiny, coup-prone Laos.
cia-0000109067: A September 1967 report on a Venezuelan university student's plans to launch anti-American action. Student radicals were the foot soldiers of Latin America's left, and campuses were organizing grounds. The entry shows the CIA tracking threats at their smallest scale — a single student's intentions, reported like weather.
cia-0000124267: A September 1957 report that Soviet artificial satellites would transmit on frequencies of 20 and 40 megacycles. Radio frequencies were practical intelligence — they told listeners where to tune in. The document is the technical fine print of the space age's opening act.
cia-0000119767: The situation in Hungary as of 5:00 PM Eastern time on October 31, 1956 — Halloween, and Budapest was celebrating a revolution that looked victorious. Soviet troops were withdrawing; Nagy's government held the capital. The document preserves the sweetest day of the uprising — four days before the end.
cia-0000126867: A March 1964 report that Zanzibar was under the control of President Karume. The revolutionary strongman had seized the island and was ruling it absolutely. The document records the consolidation: revolution's morning after, with one man holding all the guns.
cia-0000126967: A July 1968 postelection outlook for Panama. The elections had been held; the results were contested; the army was waiting. The document peers past the ballot box — and correctly senses the coup coming in October.
cia-0000132567: An October 1960 report on a Uruguayan political leader praising Castro. Not every capital was cooling — Havana still had its admirers. The document is the dissenting voice: Montevideo's left, cheering.
cia-0000132667: A 1960 report: Peru breaking diplomatic relations with Cuba. Lima made the divorce official. The document is the break: the ties, severed.
cia-0000134267: Item 11 in a 1960 Latin America series: the Castro government seeking wide distribution of propaganda — the truncated title cuts off the medium. Havana's message machine was expanding. The document is the distribution: the propaganda, spreading.
cia-0000135867: A 1952 record of a conference — both parties deleted — with attachment. The talks happened; the talkers are hidden. The entry is the gathering: the parties, unnamed — the papers, attached.
cia-0000136067: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting follow-up of opportunities in Medellin. Colombia's city held possibilities. The document is the lead: the opportunities, pursued.
cia-0000136267: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with a command message for CADICK reporting a general ultimatum to the enemy — the archive's punctuation stumbles, the truncated title cuts off the rest. The ultimatum, delivered. The entry is the demand: the enemy, warned.
cia-0000136867: A 1954 cable on a KUBARK-supported hemisphere anti-red congress scheduled for the middle of something — the truncated title cuts off when. The agency's congress. The document is the gathering: the anti-reds, convened.
cia-0000136967: A 1954 cable reporting sabotage efforts. The wrecking, reported. The document is the effort: the sabotage, chronicled.
cia-0000138967: A 1950 study of Western European political integration and ECA support — the Economic Cooperation Administration, the Marshall Plan's agency. Europe was knitting itself together with American money. The document is the project: the continent, integrating.
cia-0000139167: A 1978 file of excerpts from a daily diary — the archive's spelling says dairy — with an attached diary dated June 28. Someone's days, excerpted. The document is the diary: the entries, selected — through a typo.
un-ga-res-a-69-67: Resolution A/69/67, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The sixty-seventh act. The entry is the count: the number, the year — the rest, the text's.
un-ga-res-48-267: General Assembly Resolution 48/267, adopted in 1993 during the 48th session — aligned. The post-Cold War Assembly at work. The designation and year are preserved; the subject belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-67: Security Council Resolution 67, cataloged with the year 1947 — the numbering suggests 1949, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-367: Security Council Resolution 367, adopted in 1974. The mid-seventies Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-667: Security Council Resolution 667, adopted in 1990 — aligned. The Gulf crisis year's Council deliberated. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1567: Security Council Resolution 1567, adopted in 2004 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1767: Security Council Resolution 1767, cataloged with the year 1998 — the numbering suggests 2007, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-2667: Security Council Resolution 2667, adopted in 2022 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
cia-0000132767: A 1960 CIA file titled Cuba, numbered 0000132767. The revolution, the embargo's approach, the spies — one folder's worth. The document is the folder: the year, 1960.
cia-0000137467: A CIA situation report as of 1600 hours local time, December 10, 1961 — number 0000137467, the archive's year blank. The four-o'clock snapshot. The entry is the snapshot: the hour, 1600 — the date, December 10.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d67: The President to the Secretary of State, October 28, 1943 — Document 67. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to the department.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d167: A memorandum by the American members of the Moscow Conference committee — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 167. The American side's paper. The memo is the counterpart: the members, American.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d267: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 267. The connective passage. The note is the passage: the story, flowing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d367: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 29, 1943 — Document 367. The Allied planners, minuted again. The minutes are the again: the chiefs, combined.
the-history-of-the-reign-of-ferdinand-an: Prescott's second volume bears the Catholic Kings through the fall of Granada and the great sea ventures — Columbus's sails making Spain queen of a new world. The tale is told at the top of the historian's bent. A worthy middle to America's first great history.
arxiv-2605-08867: Picard-Lefschetz theory tracks how integrals deform as their parameters circle singularities; alien calculus resums divergent series. Si Li, Yong Li, and Xinxing Tang bring the two together in a case study, showing how the geometric and resurgent viewpoints illuminate each other. The 2026 paper is mathematical physics at the geometry-analysis interface.
arxiv-2605-09067: Tracing knee cartilage in MRI scans by hand is slow, expert work. This 2026 paper cuts that annotation burden for femoral cartilage segmentation with cross-sequence transfer learning — knowledge learned on one MRI sequence carries over to another. It is medical-imaging AI that asks less of radiologists.
arxiv-2605-09167: Speech AI speaks a few rich languages well and ignores the rest. Antonis Asonitis, Luca A. Lanzendörfer, Frédéric Berdoz, and colleagues assemble WorldSpeech, a multilingual speech corpus from around the world. The 2026 paper is data infrastructure for global voice technology.
arxiv-2605-09767: Game design pillars — the core creative constraints — emerge from mixed-initiative workflows where AI and designer collaborate. Julian Geheeb, Marvin Julian Schwarz, Daniel Dyrda, and colleagues argue LLMs are the ideal candidate for the job. The 2026 paper is AI for game design.
arxiv-2605-09867: Transformers learn online inefficiently, forgetting as they go; continuous latent contexts change the dynamics. Emile Anand, Abdullah Ateyeh, Xinyuan Cao, and colleagues enable efficient online learning in transformers. The 2026 paper is transformers that learn efficiently and continuously on the fly, always.
arxiv-2605-09967: Tensor product representation probes reveal shared structure across linear directions in neural networks — a window into how features compose. Andrew Lee and colleagues apply the probes systematically. The 2026 paper is interpretability through tensor products. It reveals the shared skeleton beneath linear directions.
arxiv-2605-10067: Jailbreaking LLMs via self-evolving metacognitive policy optimization — Metis learns to break guardrails. Huilin Zhou, Jian Zhao, Yilu Zhong, and colleagues develop the attacker. The 2026 paper is AI red-teaming automated. It evolves its own jailbreaks autonomously.
plos-pone-0003367: Published in 2008, this medical research paper traces lung damage in cystic fibrosis to a broken cellular defense. Airway cells with faulty Nrf-2 signaling stockpile too much hydrogen peroxide, a harsh chemical, and release excess IL-6, an inflammation signal. The study argues this overreaction drives the repeated lung flare-ups that gradually wear down patients' breathing.
plos-pone-0003467: Immunologists linked the cell's skeleton to its battle orders in this 2008 paper. When a T cell meets its target, actin filaments rearrange to build the immunological synapse, the contact zone where signals flow. The team showed coronin-1A ties those cytoskeleton dynamics to T-cell receptor signaling, coupling structure to the decision to attack.
plos-pone-0003567: Plant biologists found a tree's clock rewired by cold in this 2008 paper. Chestnut trees facing winter chill showed a wholesale shift in how their circadian clock genes were expressed, a cold response distinct from what herbaceous plants do. The finding reveals how woody perennials reprogram their daily rhythm to survive freezing.
plos-pone-0003667: In 2008, a team compared the insulin receptor clan by shape. The insulin receptor, the cell's docking port for insulin, its cousin IGF1R, and their relative IRR share a family build, and the team studied their outer domains side by side. The shape study maps what the three receptors share and where each goes its own way.
plos-pone-0003767: Melle, Ernst, and Schimmel taught protein patterns to tell tumors apart in this 2008 paper. Colon-derived liver metastases, primary colorectal tumors, and liver cancers each left distinct proteomic fingerprints. The protein profiles let pathologists trace a tumor back to its source.
plos-pone-0003867: Back in 2008, a group caught good cholesterol changing teams during inflammation. Acute-phase HDL, remodeled by heparan sulfate, became a novel lipoprotein with striking cholesterol-clearing power. The transformation reveals inflammation repurposing the body's lipid carriers.
plos-pone-0003967: In 2008, Brisson and Jolicœur found attention snapping back fast but awareness lagging. After misleading spatial cues, volunteers re-engaged attention quickly yet entered consciousness of targets slowly. The split timing separates attention's reflex from awareness itself.
plos-pone-0004067: In 2009, Grandison, Wong, and Bass standardized fly dieting at last. Their dietary restriction protocol ran across multiple lab strains of fruit flies. Lifespan results held steady once the method was fixed. The shared standard keeps diet-aging studies honest and comparable.
plos-pone-0004167: In 2009, Kau, Sun, and Huang turned light against anthrax. A visible-light-activated photocatalyst cut anthrax spore deaths in mice. Doped titanium dioxide worked under ordinary light, not just UV. The coating hints at self-cleaning defenses. The light-powered shield could guard hospitals and mailrooms.
plos-pone-0004267: In 2009, Budd and Campbell mapped DNA repair's precise opening cut. Mre11 nuclease teamed with Dna2 and Sgs1 in Rad51-dependent break repair. The trio trimmed broken DNA ends to start recombination. The teamwork map clarifies a core repair route at last.
plos-pone-0004367: In 2009, Oberto, Nabti, and Jooste mapped a DNA-bender's empire. The E. coli HU regulon covered genes for low oxygen, acid, salt, and SOS. The small protein commanded a broad stress army. The map reveals bacterial resilience wiring. The regulon shows one protein ruling many defenses.
plos-pone-0356767: Most pet food is built on meat or soy, but scientists are testing a protein grown from tiny organisms. This paper reports a feeding study that offered pet food made with microbial protein to dogs and cats, watching which options they chose and ate willingly. The results give a first look at whether this lab-grown protein could become a sustainable, accepted ingredient in the bowls of tomorrow.
plos-pone-0355167: Eyewitnesses get it wrong more often than courts admit. This study tested whether where a witness looks — at the eyes, nose, or mouth — predicts whether they can pick the right face from a lineup. The results feed diagnostic feature detection theory, the idea that accurate witnesses focus on the features that actually distinguish one face from another.
plos-pone-0358567: Liver tumors hide behind M2 macrophages, immune cells the cancer has co-opted. This paper reprogrammed those macrophages with TLR7/8 agonists delivered in hollow manganese dioxide nanovehicles, flipping them against the tumor. The approach slowed liver cancer progression by turning the tumor’s own guards.
plos-pone-0358767: Service demand comes in messy, over-dispersed bursts — think ER arrivals on a bad night. This paper proposed reinforced-count simulation for decision calibration under such multi-type demand. The method helps managers set staffing and resources that stay calibrated even when reality gets lumpy and unpredictable.
plos-pone-0358467: Picking the right health indicators for pigs usually happens top-down, far from the barn. This proof-of-concept compared two participatory methods — asking the people involved — for selecting pig respiratory health indicators. The comparison shows which collaborative approach picks indicators that actually work on the farm.
plos-pone-0358267: Ethiopian traditional medicine has long used Rumex abyssinicus roots — and laboratory science is catching up. This paper tested their in vitro antimicrobial potential alongside phytochemical analysis. The lab results validate the folk remedy’s germ-fighting power and identify the compounds responsible.
plos-pone-0350967: Public drug procurement in Colombia needs independent watchdogs. This paper built computational surveillance of Colombian public pharmaceutical procurement using public administrative data — a fully reproducible analysis of a closed 2020–2025 cohort. The open methods let any citizen or journalist audit where the drug money goes.
plos-pone-0357767: Melanoma is rising ominously among East Asia’s elderly. This paper tracked the disease burden from 1990 to 2023 and projected it to 2040 using machine learning. The forecasts warn health systems across the region about the wave of skin cancer cases heading their way.
plos-pone-0357567: The sugar coating on HIV’s envelope governs how the virus clumps and infects. This paper showed complex N-glycosylation governs shifts in aggregation and infectivity state of HIV-1 lentivirus with VSV-G envelope under near-physiological conditions. These glycan details matter for both gene-therapy vectors and vaccines.
plos-pone-0357667: Some people are born missing teeth — and their genes hold the explanation. This whole-exome sequencing study with cluster analysis revealed that EPB41L4A mutations may trigger tooth agenesis. The gene joins the short list of missing-tooth culprits, giving dentists and geneticists a new lead.
plos-pone-0357467: Roots feed Africa — yet research on root systems is scandalously neglected. This paper documented the research neglect of root system architecture in the root and tuber crops vital for Sub-Saharan African food security. The neglect map makes the case for funding what grows underground, not just what shows above it.
plos-pone-0357367: A single strategically placed proline can release a molecular brake on a brain receptor. This paper showed that introducing proline in the α1 M2-M3 linker relieves a brake on channel activation in α1β2γ2 GABAA receptors. The structural insight illuminates how the brain’s main inhibitory switch is fine-tuned.
plos-pone-0355967: Pumped storage hydropower plants need their control systems tested safely before going live. This paper designed, implemented, and validated a web-based dynamic simulation platform for pumped storage plant control systems. The platform lets engineers rehearse operations and failures without risking real machinery.
plos-pone-0338067: Nerve blocks for arm surgery work better and longer with the right additive. This Eritrean randomized clinical trial tested intravenous dexamethasone in supraclavicular brachial plexus block at Halibet National Referral Hospital. The trial refines anesthesia practice where resources are few but standards must stay high.
plos-pone-0357267: Seismic networks drown in waveform data of wildly uneven quality — and bad data corrupts earthquake science. This paper built a cloud-native framework for seismic waveform data quality assessment, with performance evaluated under equivalent resource constraints. The framework keeps earthquake monitoring honest by automatically flagging unreliable recordings.
plos-pone-0349467: Nursing students’ leap from classroom to hospital internship is perilous. This paper published a scoping review protocol on undergraduate nursing students’ preparedness for that transition. The planned review will map what helps students land safely — and what leaves them floundering.
plos-pone-0356467: Measuring a cell’s electrical properties usually demands an expensive, finicky patch clamp rig. This paper explored dielectrophoresis and zeta-potential measurement as potential low-cost complements for cell electrophysiology. The cheaper techniques could democratize electrical phenotyping — letting modest labs characterize cells that only elite facilities could study before.
plos-pone-0349967: Atypical respiratory pathogens — the ones standard tests miss — need dedicated surveillance. This paper described a comprehensive, innovative post-market surveillance system using an atypical-pathogen qPCR panel. The system catches the unusual bugs that slip through routine testing — before they become outbreaks.
plos-pone-0356367: Garment factories waste thread — and money — without accurate consumption forecasts. This paper built a machine learning prediction model for sewing thread consumption. The model lets manufacturers order precisely what they need — cutting waste in one of the world’s most resource-hungry industries.
plos-pone-0356267: Chlamydia reinfection plagues treatment efforts — and biomarkers could identify who’s at risk. This paper evaluated extracellular microRNAs as biomarker candidates for assessing reinfection risk. The circulating RNA signatures promise a blood test for vulnerability to repeat infection.
plos-pone-0355867: Single-cell RNA sequencing distinguishes spliced from unspliced transcripts — but quantification is tricky. This paper presented tidesurf for accurate quantification of both. The improved tool sharpens the temporal resolution of single-cell studies — letting biologists watch genes turn on and off in individual cells.
plos-pone-0354367: Nonmedical sedative and opioid use among U.S. Latinos follows social fault lines. This paper examined the social determinants driving it. The findings reveal how immigration stress, discrimination, and economic precarity shape substance use — demanding responses that address causes, not just symptoms.
plos-pone-0355367: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease — the human prion disease — needs faster diagnosis. This paper classified it using resting-state scalp EEG-derived indices. The brainwave-based classification promises earlier detection of a disease where every week of delay matters.
plos-pone-0355467: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome might be calmed through oxygen-sensing pathways. This paper showed HIF-1α inhibits the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway and modulates intestinal flora in IBS-D. The findings reveal a molecular lever connecting hypoxia responses, inflammation, and the gut microbiome.
europmc-pmc2796667: Heavy drinking and tuberculosis often appear together, but how strong is the link? This 2009 systematic review gathers the evidence on alcohol use, alcohol use disorders, and TB risk. The authors weigh study after study to estimate how much drinking raises the chance of getting and dying from TB. The review supports treating alcohol as a serious TB risk factor.
europmc-pmc2879567: Breast tissue holds many cell types, and this 2010 paper profiles them in mice and humans. The authors' transcriptome analyses of mammary cell groups reveal conserved genes and pathways. Their cross-species map aids breast cancer research. The work grounded tumor studies in normal cell biology.
europmc-pmc2966567: Medical trainees can practice on simulators before patients. This 2010 paper reviews simulation-based learning in medicine. The author argues it feels just like the real thing. Their review backed simulation training. Mannequins now bleed, breathe, and crash on cue. Mistakes on plastic beat mistakes on people.
europmc-pmc2967467: Alzheimer's unravels the brain's efficient wiring. This 2010 fMRI study finds loss of small-world networks in Alzheimer's disease through graph analysis of resting-state connectivity. The authors show the wiring frays. Their work offers a network marker. The fraying shows up before memory fails.
europmc-pmc2987867: Medical researchers need a stats primer. This 2010 paper offers a plain guide to structural equation modeling for health studies. The authors demystify the method step by step. Their primer taught a generation of students. Clinics now test cause-and-effect webs with it.
europmc-pmc3022767: Huntington's disease steals movement and mind. This 2010 review guides doctors through the inherited disorder's signs and care. The author surveys testing, drugs, and support. Their overview aids clinic teams. A single gene repeat seals the fate. Gene-silencing trials offer the first hope.
europmc-pmc3038267: Fly guts talk to ovaries about food. This 2011 paper shows gut nerves link meals to egg-making and gut upkeep in flies. The authors reveal the gut-ovary chat. Their work lights up body-wide physiology. Well-fed flies breed; starved ones wait.
europmc-pmc3042667: Heart disease needs animal stand-ins. This 2011 review surveys the main animal models of heart and vessel disease. The authors guide smart model choice. Their overview aids drug testing. Pigs' hearts mirror our own closely. Mice offer speed; pigs offer likeness.
europmc-pmc6544567: A single-letter change in a gene - a missense variant - may be harmless or disease-causing, and protein shape often decides which. Since lab-solved structures cover only part of the human proteome, this study asks whether computer-predicted 3D shapes can fill the gap. The answer: predicted structures roughly triple coverage and reliably flag risky variants.
europmc-pmc6558367: Natural killer cells decide whether to attack using KIRs - killer immunoglobulin-like receptors that read 'self' markers on other cells. This review traces KIR biology from discovery to clinic: how the receptors tune NK aggression and how doctors now exploit them in bone-marrow transplants and cancer therapy. Decades of basic science are becoming treatments.
europmc-pmc6579767: Fatty liver disease turns dangerous when simple fat buildup ignites into inflammation and scarring - the condition called NASH. In mice, researchers fingered a new trigger: ferroptosis, an iron-driven form of cell death in liver cells, which sparks the inflammatory fire. Blocking this death pathway could stop NASH before scarring sets in.
europmc-pmc6602467: Chloroplast genomes keep piling up from sequencers, and each needs its genes labeled before use. CPGAVAS2 is the upgraded web annotator that tags plastome genes, draws maps, and preps files for GenBank - fixing the reference errors that tripped its predecessor. Plant scientists get from raw sequence to annotated genome in one stop.
europmc-pmc6662567: Metagenomes are microbial soups - thousands of species' DNA jumbled together. MetaBAT 2 sorts the mess into individual genomes with an adaptive binning algorithm, faster and more robust than its popular predecessor. The tool lets researchers reconstruct genomes of microbes never grown in a lab.
europmc-pmc6679067: Gum disease is not just about teeth - it is an immune brawl, and Th17 cells throw heavy punches. This review follows the IL-23/IL-17 axis: how these signals summon tissue-wrecking inflammation in periodontitis and related diseases. Taming the axis could save both gums and joints.
europmc-pmc6712367: Stress and anxiety are tangled roommates - each stirs the other up. This review traces their shared neural circuitry: the brain systems where stress responses and anxious states overlap and interact. Untangling the biology points to treatments that could calm both at once.
europmc-pmc6735367: Stem cells calm brain inflammation - but their tiny messengers may do the real work. This study tests exosomes harvested from mesenchymal stem cells as a nano-therapy for inflammation-driven brain injury. The cell-free parcels carry the healing signal without the cells, a safer route to the same rescue.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-167: Here GAO turns its audit lens on the SEC, the Wall Street watchdog, checking the agency's own books for 2007 and 2006. Outside auditors probed its accounts, money controls, and reports to see if the numbers held up. The report gives a formal grade on the agency's finances — a neat twist, since the SEC spends its days grading everyone else's books.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-67: GAO's 2007 report finds the immigration cops needed clearer playbooks for deciding who gets sent home. With packed lockups and endless cases, officers had to pick — but the picking rules were thin. The report calls for crisp guidance so the life-changing call of removal lands the same way twice.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-67: Katrina's health billions got a GAO accounting in 2007, and the report tracks the allocation and use of the two billion for Medicaid and care. The findings follow the money. The report asks whether the sick of the storm got the help Congress sent.
openalex-w7204899567: Digoxin is one of the oldest heart drugs still in use, and this paper reviews how it treats cardiac arrhythmias, irregular heartbeats. The authors gather scientific evidence on how it is given, what it does well, its side effects, and how it affects patients' quality of life. Built as an integrative review, the article offers clinicians a current picture of a familiar medicine's place in modern heart care.
openalex-w7204536367: Brazil's ENEM exam grew from a simple high school test into the country's main gateway to college. This study traces the exam's first twenty editions: the major changes and how it became a tool for local development and for the UN's education goal, SDG 4. The authors link a national test to bigger questions of opportunity. A history of how one exam reshaped Brazilian education.
openalex-w7171801567: Some crystals push electric current sideways with no magnet in sight. This physics paper offers a new account of that odd Hall effect in flat two-layer materials, where electrons hop between energy levels. The authors blame a tiny quantum side-step. Theory work on electricity behaving badly.
pmc-13544967: A 2026 scoping review mapping what is known about the hospital experience of older adults with dementia from ethno-racial minority backgrounds and their caregivers. Hospitalization is disorienting for anyone with dementia; cultural and language barriers can deepen the harm. The review gathers the evidence and names the gaps.
pmc-13464267: This 2026 cardiology case report, "When the Wire Doesn't Come Out," describes a guidewire that could not be retrieved during a cardiac procedure and how the team handled it. Retained wires are rare but dangerous, and the paper documents the rescue strategy. It is practical reading for interventional cardiologists.
pmc-13441167: A 2026 longitudinal study of lupus patients who are serologically active but clinically quiet — blood tests show disease, but patients feel fine — examining the roles of IgG anti-dsDNA and complement C3. This discordant state puzzles rheumatologists. The study clarifies which markers predict future flares.
pmc-13469967: In this 2026 leukemia paper, ZMYM3 mutations were shown to modulate histone acetylation and cooperate with NOTCH1 mutations in chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The two mutations together drive the disease harder than either alone. The cooperation is a new therapeutic consideration.
pmc-13389067: A 2026 review on nuclear medicine in the operating room — present and future. Radioactive tracers guiding surgeons in real time is a growing field. The review maps where it stands and where it's going.
pmc-13467767: A 2026 editorial on exercise prescription, physiological mechanisms, and safety in patients with cardiac devices and arrhythmias. Exercise with a pacemaker needs guidance. The editorial sets the agenda.
pmc-13502867: This 2026 case report described EBV-induced Evans syndrome in a patient with SLE-related macrophage activation syndrome. The viral trigger complicated the autoimmune storm. The case is the lesson.
pmc-13492367: A 2026 lab-scale assessment of antievaporative lipid films as improved chemical covers for water conservation. The films slowed evaporation. The assessment is the data.
pmc-13449367: In this 2026 paper, early neurologic response predicted outcomes after anakinra for immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome. The CAR-T complication's treatment response forecasted recovery. The prediction guides care.
pmc-13598567: This 2026 Chinese-language paper developed and tested a questionnaire on health information-seeking behavior among patients with non-communicable chronic diseases — reliability and validity examined. The instrument serves health education research. The validation is the contribution.
pmc-13473867: In this 2026 randomized phase II trial, FLT-PET and FDG-PET were compared for early response assessment of neoadjuvant systemic therapy in triple-negative breast cancer (the title is truncated). The PET tracers were head-to-head. The trial is the imaging evidence.
pmc-13509367: A 2026 paper on expression profiling and transcriptional coordination of canonical Wnt signaling pathway genes (FZD2, DVL2, AXIN1) in chronic venous insufficiency. The vein disease's Wnt activity was profiled. The coordination is the finding.
pmc-13510767: This 2026 molecular biology paper showed ELAVL1 and ELAVL4 are required for Musashi-dependent translational activation. The RNA-binding proteins' cooperation was proven. The requirement is the mechanism.
pmc-13473267: A 2026 spatial transcriptomics paper revealing injury-responsive compartments and coordinated immune-fibrotic signaling in ANCA-associated renal vasculitis. The kidney's injury zones were mapped. The revealing is the pathologic insight.
pmc-13436567: In this 2026 paper, astragalin suppressed colorectal carcinogenesis by targeting proliferation, oxidative stress, and inflammation. The plant flavonoid fought colon cancer on three fronts. The suppressing is the mechanism.
pmc-13432867: A 2026 comprehensive review of host-orf virus interactions — pathogenesis and immune evasion mechanisms. The zoonotic virus's biology was surveyed. The review is the reference.
pmc-13465767: This 2026 prostate cancer paper showed adipose dysfunction caused by obesity and radiation therapy rewired the prostate stroma toward tumor progression. The fat-radiation-stroma axis was decoded. The rewiring is the mechanism.
pmc-13431967: A 2026 paper on injectable artificial photoreceptors — stem cell functional integration and in vivo electrophysiological validation in retinal degeneration models. The artificial retinas integrated. The validation is the regenerative advance.
pmc-13550467: In this 2026 paper, analysis of deep-resequencing data of 984 soybean accessions revealed structural variations underlying agronomic traits. The soybean's structural diversity was mapped. The revealing serves breeding.
pmc-13511467: In this 2026 sleep medicine paper, targeting hypoglossal neurobiology in obstructive sleep apnea treatment was examined — the emergence of aroxybutynin-atomoxetine (AD109). The drug combo's mechanism was explained. The emergence is the therapeutic hope.
pmc-13447667: In this 2026 cryo-EM methods paper, integrating multitemperature sample preparation with particle rebalancing addressed preferred orientation. The orientation bias was corrected. The integrating is the technical advance.
pmc-13449967: A 2026 protocol for high-resolution mapping of RNA-associated chromatin using chromatin isolation by RNA purification-tag. The RNA-chromatin mapping was the method. The protocol enables new experiments.
arxiv-2606-16167: AI systems are mostly built by and for a narrow slice of humanity. This paper argues for AI pluralism: the idea that AI should reflect many cultures, values, and worldviews — and examines the worlds current AI misses. It is a philosophical and policy-oriented piece, aimed at researchers thinking about whose perspectives AI serves.
arxiv-2606-16367: Two crowds that shove while they roam split turf — think rival fans in a plaza. This paper proves split-turf answers live for crowd-flow math with fade-out spread and stray pulls. For flow-math fans who model turf wars. Proofs pin down when the split holds.
arxiv-2606-16667: See-say bots at times opine when they should bow out — and bow out when they could opine. This paper makes them peek again before they bow: reap proof on a purse, with vow-backed odds. For see-say crews who want bots to own their edge.
arxiv-2606-16867: Humans handle 'not' effortlessly — 'not happy' flips meaning. Do AI models? This paper revisits systematicity in negation in the era of in-context learning: whether models handle 'not' consistently. It is for linguists and NLP researchers probing model logic. Small word, big trouble.
